_purpose: Machine-readable definition of ORIGINAL vs CURRENT NyayaMind prototype configurations for the final_comparison evaluation. Both configs run through the IDENTICAL pipeline code (src/pipeline.py etc.) -- this is a configuration A/B, not a code-fork A/B, except for the claim-parser ablation (section parser_ablation) which is a genuine pre-fix/post-fix code diff, documented separately.
derivation: Every value below is copied verbatim from research/prototype/config/prototype.yaml (as committed) and cross-checked against FINAL_PRODUCTION_CONFIG.md and REPRODUCIBILITY.md §5. Nothing here was invented for this comparison.

ORIGINAL.label: pre-2026-08-27 production baseline
ORIGINAL.description: The configuration under which every historical output in outputs/ committed before 2026-08-27 was produced (run_A/B/C_n30, run_natural_targeted, run_synthetic_stress, natural_candidates_50_gpu, natural_candidates_batch2_gpu, and Arm A of final_gpu_validation).
ORIGINAL.claim_parser_version: current (post commit 223eb9d) for the primary ORIGINAL baseline used in this comparison (final_gpu_validation Arm A, batch1/batch2 bare-v0 runs). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the very earliest n=30/targeted experiments (run_A/B/C_n30, run_natural_targeted, commit 0e37525) predate commit 223eb9d and DID use the pre-fix parser -- those are NOT used as the primary ORIGINAL baseline here; the claim_parser ablation below (parser_ablation pair) isolates that earlier fix separately.
ORIGINAL.citation_identity_preservation_on_correc: always on -- core pipeline logic, not a toggle, identical in ORIGINAL and CURRENT
ORIGINAL.sibling_regression_protection: not applicable -- only activates when atomic_scope_check is truthy; inactive under ORIGINAL by construction

CURRENT.label: shipped production config, decided 2026-08-27
CURRENT.description: research/prototype/config/prototype.yaml exactly as committed. Decision record: FINAL_PRODUCTION_CONFIG.md.
CURRENT.citation_identity_preservation_on_correc: always on -- core pipeline logic, not a toggle, identical in ORIGINAL and CURRENT
CURRENT.sibling_regression_protection: active whenever atomic_scope_check is truthy -- always active under CURRENT

unchanged_between_ORIGINAL_and_CURRENT: citation-identity preservation on correction (_citation_identity(), always on)
the ENTAILED-only shipping gate: status=='corrected' iff reverification.verdict=='ENTAILED'

isolated_ab_pairs_actually_run_in_this_r.note: Because premise_framing, use_evidence_v1, atomic_scope_check and narrow_reverification_hypothesis were each validated independently before being combined, the strongest evidence for THIS comparison is a set of controlled pairs, each changing the minimum number of variables needed to isolate one lever. This project has never run a single experiment that flips ALL FOUR levers from ORIGINAL to CURRENT simultaneously on one fresh natural batch with real GPU generation -- that gap is stated explicitly wherever it matters below and in FINAL_BASELINE_COMPARISON.md.

pairs.name: premise_framing_ablation_controlled_benchmark
pairs.note: Curated adversarial benchmark, not natural NyayaRAG data -- see final_demo_pack for construction methodology.

pairs.name: premise_framing_ablation_natural_cpu_reverify
held_fixed: same 147 already-matched claims from final_gpu_validation Arm B

pairs.name: scope_check_ablation_deterministic_replay
held_fixed: the actual Qwen-generated correction text (replayed, not regenerated)
pairs.note: Deterministic re-check of the scope-violation RULE against already-generated correction text -- no new model call.

pairs.name: evidence_corpus_ablation_corpuslevel
held_fixed: all 588 already-extracted claims pooled from every natural experiment's generated text
pairs.note: Corpus-level, not paired-arm; complements the paired GPU retrieval_ablation above with a larger claim pool.

pairs.name: claim_parser_ablation_n30_reparse
held_fixed: same evidence pool version used at time of comparison
pairs.note: Claim segmentation itself changes (88 -> 93 claims) because the fix affects what counts as a claim boundary -- not a strict 1:1 paired-claim comparison; compared as coverage-of-claims-extracted-from-same-cases.

never_jointly_measured: All four CURRENT levers (v1 evidence + labeled framing + assertion_spans + narrow_reverification) enabled together vs. ORIGINAL, on one fresh, never-before-seen natural GPU batch, in a single paired run. The closest approximation is chaining: final_gpu_validation Arm A (ORIGINAL) -> Arm B (+v1/+scope/+narrow, still bare) -> labeled CPU re-verification of Arm B's claims (+labeled) -> labeled_correction_validation_gpu (+labeled correction path) -- four separate, real, paired/chained experiments on the SAME 50-case batch, not one combined run from a single fresh generation.

explicitly_out_of_scope.baseline/LegalSeg: A separate git submodule reproducing RhetoricLLaMA for rhetorical-role segmentation -- a different task (sentence-level rhetorical labeling, not statutory-claim verification) on a different dataset. Not a comparable 'original NyayaMind' baseline for this claim-verification prototype and is not touched or compared here.
explicitly_out_of_scope.lawyer_ground_truth: Does not exist anywhere in this project. All verdict-agreement numbers against assumption_annotation.jsonl or lawyer_annotation.jsonl are PROVISIONAL (Claude-generated labels) and are kept out of every headline metric in this comparison.
